perf.summary: First(n,k) and Second(n,k) generate the entire row via FirstRow/SecondRow (O(n^2) work) just to return a single entry row[k]; if many single-entry queries are made this is wasteful, and the row buffer is discarded.
perf.currentCost: O(n^2) modular mults to fill row[0..n], then return one element; buffer freed immediately.
perf.proposedChange: Document that First/Second are O(n^2) single-shot helpers and expose the existing FirstRow/SecondRow (already public) as the batched API for callers needing multiple k; optionally early-out the inner UpdateSecondRow/UpdateFirstRow to stop maintaining indices > k is NOT valid (recurrence needs full row), so the real win is API guidance: prefer FirstRow when more than one k is queried for the same n.
perf.rationale: No cheaper algorithm exists for a single Stirling number than building the row, so the win is ergonomic/purity: steer batch callers to the row API to avoid recomputing the whole O(n^2) row per k. Prevents quadratic-per-query blowup in loops.
perf.risk: Ergonomic guidance only; no behavior change. If kept as-is it is already correct. Mark low-priority.

perf.summary: factor is recomputed via two nested % operations though (i-1) < MOD for all realistic i, making the outer reductions redundant.
perf.currentCost: ((long)MOD - ((long)(i-1) % MOD)) % MOD per row: two modulo ops where i-1 is a small loop index almost always < MOD.
perf.proposedChange: long factor = (long)(MOD - (i - 1)); when i-1 < MOD (guaranteed when n < MOD, the normal case), giving the negative-coefficient directly without the inner %; keep the general form only if i-1 can exceed MOD.
perf.rationale: Removes two modulo operations per row (n total) on a value that is provably in [0,MOD) under the normal n<MOD precondition, replacing with a single subtraction.
perf.risk: Valid only if i-1 < MOD (i.e. n <= MOD). Since these tables are stackalloc'd of size n+1 and MOD is a large prime, n<MOD effectively always holds; state this guard. If n could exceed MOD, keep one % on (i-1).
